The systematic equity trading strategy for India's market will focus on short-horizon mean reversion. The economic mechanism exploits the tendency of stock prices to revert to historical averages after significant deviations. This persistence can be attributed to investor psychology, market inefficiencies, and information delays.

To exploit this, the rule would identify stocks that have experienced extreme price movements (either positively or negatively) relative to their historical volatility. These stocks are then shorted if overvalued or bought if undervalued, with trades held for a few days to capture mean reversion effects. The strategy will use technical indicators such as Bollinger Bands and average true range to define entry and exit points, ensuring timely execution of the trade before the price returns to its mean.

The signal for this systematic equity strategy involves computing Bollinger Bands and Average True Range (ATR) indicators using daily open, high, low, close prices. For Bollinger Bands, calculate the 20-day simple moving average (SMA) of the closing price as the central line, with upper and lower bands set at 2 standard deviations from the SMA. Rank stocks based on their current price relative to these bands: those below the lower band are considered undervalued candidates for long positions, while those above the upper band are seen as overvalued candidates for short positions.

For ATR, calculate the 14-day moving average of true ranges (the highest of high-to-low range, high-to-close range, and close-to-low range) to measure market volatility. Use this to filter out stocks with very low or very high volatility that might not exhibit mean reversion tendencies as expected. On a given day, rank the candidates by their Bollinger Band positions adjusted for ATR values, prioritizing those showing clear signs of mean reversion potential.

The systematic equity strategy will hold positions in up to 30 stocks at any given time, with weights dynamically adjusted based on mean reversion potential. Long positions receive a weight of 2% each if undervalued, while short positions get a corresponding -2%. This limits total exposure to 60% long and 60% short across the portfolio. To manage risk, absolute drawdowns are capped at 15%, ensuring that losses do not exceed this threshold. Positions are exited when stocks revert to their Bollinger Bands or ATR criteria no longer indicate mean reversion opportunities.
